source: Prek Leap National School of Agriculture - "Banana Varieties Giving High Yield and Good Taste Quality" (ពូជចេកផ្តល់ទិន្នផលខ្ពស់ និងគុណភាពសជាតិ) variety trial report, January 2007
text:
On yield and eating quality, the trial's conclusion highlights specific standout accessions rather than reporting every variety's raw numbers (which are not transcribed here - see the growth-measurements entry for the same caution about numeric-table legibility). Accession #18 (FHIA-21) produced notably long, good-quality fruit. Accession #13 (SH 3436-9) had a high number of well-formed fruit per bunch, but accession #15 (TMBx 5295-1, second accession) produced the single heaviest bunch weight recorded in the trial.

On taste, accessions #4, #7, #10 and #20 (FHIA-03, Aacv Rose, FHIA-17, and FHIA-25) were noted for good, well-balanced sweetness, while #15 had a milder sweetness comparable to the ripe-fruit taste of some local varieties. The report also notes that a portion of accessions produced fruit of only ordinary size and weight (about 5% of accessions) and fruit with a bland, non-aromatic taste (about 35% of accessions) - meaning that, while several imported lines showed strong potential, taste and size were not automatically better than local varieties across the whole set, and any recommendation to farmers should be based on the specific named standout varieties above rather than "imported varieties" as a blanket category.
